findings.title: AIAgent construction sits outside the worker try/finally
findings.description: In _run_contractor_agent_sync the AIAgent(...) constructor runs before _set_active_contractor_agent and before the try/finally that performs _cleanup_agent_resources(agent, reraise=True). If the constructor itself raises, the partially built agent is never registered or cleaned up.
findings.impact: Negligible in practice: AIAgent.__init__ is allocation/configuration only and acquires resources lazily, so a constructor failure leaks nothing live; worst case is an un-cleaned partial object that gets garbage collected.
findings.required_fix: Optional hardening: wrap construction so a constructor exception still routes the partial agent (if bound) through _cleanup_agent_resources, or document the lazy-resource invariant next to the constructor call.

findings.title: Lazy lock fallback in _set_active_contractor_agent is itself racy
findings.description: The defensive fallback that creates _contractor_agents_lock/_contractor_agents via getattr when missing performs check-then-set without synchronization; two threads could install different locks if __init__ initialization were ever bypassed (as in object.__new__ tests).
findings.impact: None in production: GatewayRunner.__init__ (run.py:7701-7702) always initializes both attributes before any contractor turn can run, so the fallback is dead defensive code.
findings.required_fix: Optional: drop the lazy fallback (fail fast on uninitialized runner) or accept it as test-only scaffolding; no change required for this gate.
